newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening sharply lower.

text.p: Stocks were expected to meet with heavy selling at Wednesday's opening, pressured by a series of reports and rumours that called into question the recent strength of blue chips and technology stocks.

Analysts said the market, which has again showed fierce resilience following a sharp sell-off last Friday, would be tested once more by rumours that International Business Machines Corp. was about to issue a profit warning.

There were also concerns about a column in the Wall Street Journal questioning whether Japanese institutions were losing their appetite for U.S. Treasuries, which sent the bond market down at its opening.
"It looks like a very rough morning," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.

Regarding the Wall Street Journal report, which appeared in its Heard on the Street column, Wachtel said, "We've seen these stories time and time again, but because this one comes from (Goldman Sachs International Vice Chairman Robert) Hormats, it carries some weight."
U.S. Treasuries were weaker in early activity, with the 30-year bond off 20/32 to yield 6.54 percent, up from 6.49 percent Tuesday.
Analysts said blue chips and tech stocks were vulnerable to a corrective sell-off because of their recent strength.
Perhaps most vulnerable is IBM, which has staged a huge rally in the past month.
An IBM spokesman told Reuters the company had no comment on the profit warning rumours. However, he said IBM had no plans to issue a press release Wednesday.
"There are grumblings about an IBM earnings warning," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, "and it's clear IBM would be clobbered if that's the case."
"I expect a sharply lower opening and I would not rule out a drop like Friday," he said "It's possible we could see the Dow dropping as much as 150 points during the day."
